summary: Current main still passes missing CPU metadata from speculative extend into the FlashInfer FP4 dequant workspace. A focused regression reproduced the resulting NoneType failures. This change adds a narrow boundary check that replaces them with an actionable RuntimeError; it does not claim to make NVFP4 speculative decoding graph-safe. Upstream PRs #36038 and #36045 remain the existing architecture-specific full-fix candidates.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before run against the original implementation reproduced unhandled None metadata failures; raw output is reports/j-f4f0d0a6ae8e/failing-before.log.

Passing-after regression: 2 tests passed, including three subtests independently omitting request indices, prefix lengths, and extend lengths, plus an empty valid metadata boundary. Raw output is reports/j-f4f0d0a6ae8e/passing-after.log.
Patch whitespace and Python bytecode compilation.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned single GPU is AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The reported path requires NVIDIA SM120, CUDA FlashInfer/TRTLLM NVFP4 support, and the Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 weights. Hardware inventory is retained in reports/j-f4f0d0a6ae8e/gpu-environment.log; no unrelated GPU smoke is counted as issue validation.

remaining_limitations: The original RTX 5090/SM120 full-model eager and CUDA Graph serving reproductions were not run because this job provides gfx950 ROCm hardware and not the reported model weights.
The defensive check improves failure diagnosis only; it does not supply the graph-safe FP4 speculative attention path needed to solve the serving bug.

Upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36038 routes speculative phases through TRTLLM MHA native FP4 decode, while https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36045 implements a GPU-resident FlashInfer workspace. Both are open and neither is present in the recorded base.
Ruff was not installed in the prepared interpreter; compileall and git diff --check passed.
